newsitem.title: USA: Suspects escape from new police building.
newsitem.headline: Suspects escape from new police building.

text.p: City police said Wednesday they were checking security at their newly-renovated headquarters after two suspected criminals managed to slip out of the building unnoticed.

"It's like any other new building, we knew there would be some bugs to work out," said Pam Alejandre, spokeswoman for the Sacramento Police Department. "But obviously this was not one of the bugs we wanted to discover."

The first escape occurred over the weekend when a man arrested for the suspected stabbing murder of his father managed to open the door of his holding cell and walk out of the building. Alejandre said it appeared the door of the cell did not align with the frame, preventing the bolt from catching when police thought they were locking the suspect inside.
A few days later a man being held on attempted rape charges used the chair in his cell to break the lock.
Both men were arrested within hours of their escapes and the suspected murderer has since been charged with the crime.
The new headquarters building was formerly a bank which underwent a $3.5 million renovation before the police moved in.
